findings.title: Inventive step: the only purpose-specific effect is not shown by the application's own data
findings.attack: [0287] reports cured sealant film on the seat-ring outer surface in the purge-gap region, the surface the air purge is said to clean. The clean surfaces are those swept by the main passage and the snap-back wipe, and [0140]/[0289] say the test does not isolate the two. The problem is recast as a second flow path at a higher differential: US4044791A (secondary passageways opened by further travel against a second spring) or US5918628A, combined with US5924444A (ring deformed radially outward to open a gap, returning on closing), with mechanical actuation treated as common general knowledge.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Add disclosure on the purge flow route over the seat-ring outer surface, why film remains there, and any observation separating the two cleaning actions. Otherwise restate the effect ([0013], [0016], [0139]) around what Example 1 shows (clean sealing surfaces, no failure in 40 cycles against 12/14/18). No claim narrowing proposed.

findings.title: Claim 3 seat ring is distinguished from undulating tubular metal seats only by its intended use
findings.attack: The poppet, over-travel and purge gap are not part of the claimed article. What remains is a tubular ring with a sealing edge at one end and a wall that grows radially under axial load and recovers. US11549591B1 FIG. 10 shows a resilient metal seat element 812 with a cylindrical sidewall 814 and undulating flanges forming the seat for poppet 804; under [0061] a wall not straight in section is 'convoluted'. US: intended use does not distinguish a capable structure. EPO/UK: 'for' means suitable for; EP3171056A1 (wave-section ring whose flattening moves it radially) supplies the conversion. Claims 4 and 86 (standard NiTi shape-setting, US9126251B2) and 62-64 fall with it.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Add to claim 3 that the wall's outer surface, with a bore surrounding the seat ring, bounds the purge gap (claim 65, [0124], statement 4.1), and that the load-converting geometry lies between the sealing edge and the opposite end ([0167]). The through-wall purge of claim 67 then needs its own route.

findings.title: "Closed at rest" is defined so that it has no limiting content
findings.attack: [0067] makes every gap 'closed' at rest (rest position, no gas-tightness required), and the FIG. 4A instruction shows a clearance at rest against [0187]'s line contact. US 112(b). EPO/UK: under G 1/24 claim 1 reads on a deflection that merely widens an existing clearance (cf. US5924444A gap 314), dissolving the [0013]/[0065] distinction.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Redefine by function (contact, or within a stated clearance, no substantial flow at rest). Exclude a clearance that already passes flow. Correct the FIG. 4A instruction. Needs the inventor's confirmation.

findings.title: Subject matter recorded as unconfirmed candidates is drawn and claimed
findings.attack: figures.md records FIGS. 11, 12 and 13A as 'not stated in the inventor's disclosure … pending inventor confirmation', and the FIG. 4 fit band as a drafting resolution. The design-around dependents directed to them are exposed on inventorship: Thaler v. Vidal (US), [2023] UKSC 49 (UK), J 8/20 (EPO).
findings.least_narrowing_action: Inventor confirmation per candidate. Keep what is confirmed; delete what is not, or record the real contributor. Strip the provenance captions.

findings.title: Background attributes content to a publication number that the record marks as fictional
findings.attack: The prior-art index lists 'US2019/0123456A1' only as requester item S1, a fictional test reference never fetched. If filed, the description misstates a real publication (37 CFR 1.56), and at the EPO/UK the text stands as an admission that the listed features were known, usable against the dependent claims.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Delete [0007], or restate it without a number only if the inventor or counsel confirms it. Recheck [0013].

findings.title: Normal stroke and over-travel are defined by the contact itself, so claim 1 has no independent travel limitation
findings.attack: [0071]/[0072] define the boundary as the first contact, so 'spaced … throughout the normal stroke' is true by definition. Claim 1 is not tied to the two thresholds of claim 5 and reads on a single-rate poppet that at full lift pushes a compliant element opening a bypass, which eases the F-32-1 combination.
findings.least_narrowing_action: In [0071], also mark the end of the normal stroke by an independent structural feature (change of rate [0122] or stop [0151]). Fallback: fold claim 5 into claim 1. That is narrowing; it gives up travel not produced by a separate over-travel differential.

findings.title: Snap-back wipe cannot occur in the sequence the description gives
findings.attack: Per [0137] the seat ring recovers when the purge shoulder lifts, before the poppet returns through the normal stroke, so the sealing face is still about 0.6 mm away. A radial return of at most 0.15 mm cannot carry the ring 'across the sealing face'. [0138] offers only a belief. US 112(a); EPO Art 83 and clarity for these claims.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Have the inventor state the actual wipe geometry (what is near the ring at recovery; whether the wipe acts on the purge shoulder), then reword [0085], [0138] and the claims. Otherwise delete the wipe from the claims.

findings.title: The two-piece seat is not described as opening a purge gap
findings.attack: The two-piece seat text says only that the wiper ring 144 is deflected outward and wipes. No purge gap, location or air route is described, numeral 146 (claim 1) is absent from the description, and nothing explains how the purge shoulder passes the rigid seat 140 on which the same poppet seals. US written description of this species under claim 1; EPO reference signs pointing to an undescribed feature.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Add to [0181]-[0182] the purge gap 146 between wiper ring 144 and core body bore 22, its closure at rest and opening, its air route into the tyre chamber 80, and how the purge shoulder reaches the wiper ring past the rigid seat. Inventor to confirm.

findings.title: Principal-embodiment geometry: axial load path and purge-flow route are not stated consistently
findings.attack: A purge shoulder on the poppet can reach the seat ring only at the end away from the sealing edge, which is the retained fit-band end (as the FIG. 2 instruction says), whereas [0113] says the load is applied 'at its upper edge', the sealing edge. The text does not say what reacts the load so that it passes through the convoluted wall, nor how pump-side air enters an annular gap closed on one side by the interference-fitted fit band. On the text alone this raises 112(a)/Art 83 doubts about the only built embodiment, and 112(b)/Art 84 points on 'upper' and 'below'.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Add an inventor-confirmed paragraph stating the seat-ring orientation, the side and end the purge shoulder contacts, what reacts the axial load, and the purge-gap inlet and outlet. Align [0113] and the FIG. 2 instruction.

findings.title: Sufficiency across the breadth of the genus claims
findings.attack: One built species. [0210] concedes spring-tempered metal is not proposed for a continuous convoluted wall, yet claims 20-26 have no material limit. [0290] gives no PEEK gap width. UK breadth sufficiency; EPO Art 83; US Wands.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Add material guidance within the inventor's conception (minimum recoverable strain; PEEK estimate) and recast [0210] as that guidance. Narrowing by material is the last resort and gives up non-NiTi metal seat rings.

findings.title: Functional genus terms invite a US 112(f) construction
findings.attack: Generic nouns plus function, reinforced by [0106]. A US court may limit each term to the disclosed structures and equivalents, with indefiniteness if the linkage is unclear.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Add non-narrowing structural content to each term and list the linked structures in [0106], or accept the 112(f) reading in the US.

findings.title: Second independent valve-core claim (claim 77), unity a posteriori, and US restriction
findings.attack: Claim 77 is a second independent valve-core claim outside claim 1 (Rule 43(2) EPC). If claim 3 is read as in F-32-2, claims 1-2 and 3-4 share no special technical feature (Art 82). US restriction among claims 1-4 is likely.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Recast claim 77 as dependent on claim 20 via the seat ring of claim 3, or delete it. Align claim 3 with claim 1 (F-32-2).

findings.title: Claims 45, 49 and 50 are defined by, or contradict, entities outside the claimed category
findings.attack: Claim 45 bounds a valve-core feature by the valve stem. Claim 49 contradicts claim 47's 'received in a bore'. Claim 50 defines a tyre valve by the sealant in the tube. US 112(b)/(d); EPO Art 84.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Move claim 45 under claim 47. Amend claim 47 to 'received in, or formed in, the valve stem'. Recast claim 50 as a tyre-chamber claim per [0327].

findings.title: US multiple-dependency form and claims fees in all three offices
findings.attack: US: multiple dependent claims resting on multiple dependent claims are improper (35 USC 112(e), 37 CFR 1.75(c)) and not examined; proper ones carry a surcharge. EPO claims fees from claim 16, higher from 51. UK fee over 25. 86 claims.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Prepare a US single-dependency set. Consolidate range and material fallbacks with description basis in [0240]-[0249].

findings.title: Drawings: FIG. 13A undescribed, numerals missing from the description, text legends in captions
findings.attack: FIG. 13A and numeral 220 are not in the description (37 CFR 1.74; Rule 42(1)(d) EPC). Numeral 146 (claim 1) is not in the description. Provenance captions are non-indispensable text (Rule 46(2)(f) EPC) and advertise F-32-4.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Describe FIG. 13A once confirmed, or drop and renumber. Introduce 146. Reduce captions to view titles.

findings.title: Method claim 2 is performed by the end user
findings.attack: The steps are performed by a cyclist inflating a tyre, not by a valve-core maker, who is at most an indirect infringer (US inducement or contributory infringement; UK s.60(2)). An enforcement weakness, not a rejection ground.
findings.least_narrowing_action: None to claim 2. Rely on claims 1, 3 and 47. Counsel may consider a valve core supplied with over-travel inflation instructions ([0276]), subject to printed-matter limits.

findings.title: Purge gap width range is claimed for every radially deflectable element
findings.attack: [0237] states the range for the seat-ring purge gap 60 and ties it to flattening of convolution 36. Claim 19, through claim 16, applies it to the slotted sleeve, split and tapered rings and wiper ring, which have no stated width. A US written-description question and an intermediate-generalisation risk for EPO amendments.
findings.least_narrowing_action: If the inventor agrees, state in [0237] that the range applies to any radially deflectable element. Otherwise make claim 19 depend on claims 20-26.

findings.title: Relative orientation terms without a frame of reference
findings.attack: 'Below' has no reference when the axial views are drawn with the valve axis horizontal. Claim 14 does not use the [0117] gloss.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Use 'spaced from the sealing face along the axis of the poppet' in claim 14, and define 'upper' in [0112].

findings.title: Convolution amplitude claimed where no convolution is required
findings.attack: Through claim 3 the geometry may be a strut pattern or helical slot with no convolution, leaving the amplitude alternative without a referent.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Limit the amplitude alternative of claim 68, and claim 69, to dependency on claims 62-67; keep the other dimensions on claim 3.

findings.title: Approximate and nominal values in claims
findings.attack: 'About' and 'nominal' invite an EPO clarity objection. [0056] gives no tolerance figure.
findings.least_narrowing_action: State a tolerance in [0250]/[0259], or delete the terms in the European set.

assumptions.text: A1. Common general knowledge: a thin resilient undulating or bowed wall under axial compression changes diameter and recovers when unloaded.
A2. Common general knowledge (examiner's likely position): mechanical actuation of a seal element in place of flow actuation is an ordinary design alternative.
A3. No abstract, no priority document and no drawings in the package; the figure instructions were read as the drawings' content.
A4. Patent eligibility raises no objection in any of the three jurisdictions.
A5. The saved prior art is thin by its own index; a fuller search (CN/TW/DE utility models) could produce stronger references.

open_questions.text: Q1. At rest, does the prototype seat ring touch the bore along its free portion, or is there a clearance?
Q2. How does the air purge act on the purge-gap surfaces, and why did film remain there?
Q3. Which end of the seat ring does the purge shoulder contact, what reacts the load, and where does air enter the purge gap?
Q4. What does the seat ring actually wipe on recovery, given the sealing face is 0.6 mm away?
Q5. Which candidate constructions (FIGS. 4, 11, 12, 13A; claim 15 collar) did the inventor conceive?
Q6. Is the content of [0007] true of any real document or product?
